newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson Q2 professional sales up.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson Q2 professional sales up.

text.p: Health care products giant Johnson & Johnson said Tuesday its second-quarter professional, pharmaceutical and consumer sales were each more than four percent higher than the same period a year ago.

The company said in a statement that global professional sales totaled $2.15 billion, six percent more than the same period last year. Domestic sales were 7.5 percent higher, while international ones were 4.3 percent higher, it said.
Vistakon's disposable contact lenses and Ethicon Endo-Surgery's minimally invasive surgical instruments were some of the products that helped the growth in sales, it added.

The company said worldwide pharmaceutical sales totaled $1.93 billion for the quarter, 7.0 percent higher than the same period last year. Domestic sales were 13.6 percent higher, while international sales were 1.4 percent higher.
Antipsychotic medication Risperdal and anemia treatment Procrit were some of the drugs that led the increase in pharmaceutical sales, it said.
Johnson & Johnson said its worldwide consumer segment had sales of $1.61 billion, 4.4 percent more than the same period a year ago.
"Sales were led by the strong performance of over-the-counter pharmaceuticals and the continued strength of our skin care franchise, including the NEUTROGENA line of products," it said.
The company reported a profit of $0.68 a share for the second quarter, 13 percent more than the same period in 1996.
Sales totaled $5.70 billion against $5.38 billion a year ago, it added.
